params.developerInstructions:
You translate the supplied natural-language proof faithfully into Lean 4. Use the explicit project premises and any proved result in the pinned Mathlib environment. Preserve all assumptions, conclusions, equality modes and the supplied proof route. No reference answers, personal context, other tasks, shell or external services are available. Use the submit tool when the requested artifact is complete; if rejected, repair it. A strategy is advice, never an additional theorem or assumption.

# Lean implementation safeguards

Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.

1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
   unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
   environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
   side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
   when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
   its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
   A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
   obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
   type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
   or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
   unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
   implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
   representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
   it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
   check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
   A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
   not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
   fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
   requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
   application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
   to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
   more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
   `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
   use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
   the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
   obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.

5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
   limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
   A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
   control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
   then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
   integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
   limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
   requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.

The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.

Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
`#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.
 A native resource failure may include repair_advice from frozen ST020. Use its applicable diagnostic branch first, repair in this same stage and recheck the unchanged target. Advice does not add assumptions or establish acceptance. End this stage immediately when a submit tool reports stage_complete:true; the controller handles later stages. Within a proof stage, checked helper attempts are available through read_lean_draft. After a context reset, query its index before claiming no draft or helper exists. Helpers never become new premises. If the fixed interface or source appears inconsistent, report_proof_obstruction with located actual evidence instead of silently changing it or repeating a blocker. Compiler/interface reports require a relevant failed own-context check; successful helpers or bare inability are insufficient. Rejected reports leave you active. Ordinary proof-body errors remain your local repair work. The controller routes the reported issue; it does not change frozen endpoints or retire sibling work on an idle-turn counter. Use familiar interfaces directly; no background-note scan is required. For a relevant obstacle, select a matching local background_note_index entry and read_background_note if its details may help. Relate the actual Lean goal/context to its NL step: use the note grounds to identify a small missing application premise or transport, prove it from permitted inputs, then check the intended application. Verify actual types and conditions; a note is not a Lean proof or extra assumption. If it does not fit, continue ordinary allowed search or repair without insisting on that note or rebuilding a larger argument by default.

dynamicTools.name: search_mathlib
dynamicTools.description: Search the pinned mathlib Lean source using a regular expression; at most 100 lines.

dynamicTools.name: read_mathlib
dynamicTools.description: Read specified lines of a Mathlib/*.lean source file from the pinned checkout.

dynamicTools.name: check_transition
dynamicTools.description: Compile a tactic body for the fixed target; no leading by, declarations, or placeholders.

dynamicTools.name: submit_transition
dynamicTools.description: Submit and check the final tactic body for the same target.

dynamicTools.name: check_auxiliary
dynamicTools.description: Compile one helper proposition and tactic body in exactly this local port context. This never accepts the final goal or adds a premise.

dynamicTools.name: read_lean_draft
dynamicTools.description: Read only your own same-stage proof/helper attempts. kind=index lists attempts; proof/auxiliary returns the selected body lines and actual check. No other stage or file is accessible.

dynamicTools.name: report_proof_obstruction
dynamicTools.description: Escalate an observed obstruction for serial diagnosis. Reference resolving JSON pointers in your current packet and at most six actual own proof/helper attempts. Alleging an interface/source error grants no premise or acceptance. Do not keep repeating inability messages: use this tool. Ordinary proof errors should first be repaired locally.

dynamicTools.name: read_background_note
dynamicTools.description: Read one complete audited background note from this task index by its qualified ID. No other task, file or proof is accessible; this is guidance, not a checked Lean proof.

{"task": "Prove exactly this local conditional obligation using the supplied NL route. Return only the tactic body through submit_transition. All displayed parameter and input proof binders are already in context.", "packet": {"version": 2, "contract_sha256": "84f26158cde742dbfac2a828a2dcadf40e9a9c0f9647c7712e9fb31b9f596384", "header": "import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
abbrev Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
instance ratComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance (priority := 50) localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance (priority := 50) localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ

def Preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, f (m : V) ∈ M
def RPreserves (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ localizedImage p M, f u ∈ localizedImage p M
structure LatticeOps (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  x : Module.End ℤ M
  y : Module.End ℤ M
  h : Module.End ℤ M
  X : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  Y : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
def Agrees (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (a : LatticeOps M) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : M, (a.x m : V) = x (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.y m : V) = y (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.h m : V) = h (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.X r m : V) = divided x r (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.Y r m : V) = divided y r (m : V))
def Invariant {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (f : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, f u ∈ W
def Simple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Invariant W x → Invariant W y → Invariant W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Highest (lam : ℤ) (x h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (lam : ℂ) • w
def Admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℤ M) (c : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (b i : V) = c i) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r)
def extendFamily {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (i : ℕ) : U :=
  if hi : i < lam.toNat + 1 then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def GeneratorFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Index lam,
    x (b i) = (if i.val = 0 then 0 else
      (((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - 1))) ∧
    y (b i) = ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + 1) ∧
    h (b i) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def DividedFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Index lam) (r : ℕ),
    X r (b i) = (if r ≤ i.val then
      ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - r)
      else 0) ∧
    Y r (b i) = ((Nat.choose (i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + r)
def E (lam : ℤ) (b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def MatrixWord {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End F U :=
  ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : F)⁻¹) •
    (X (lam.toNat - i.val) * (Y lam.toNat * X lam.toNat) * Y (lam.toNat - j.val))
def BasisLift (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M),
    ∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val
def Principal (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  b ≠ 0 ∧ J p M y v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a ∧
    Simple (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)


def Lowering (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℕ,
    h ((y ^ t) v) = (((lam - 2 * (t : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
    x ((y ^ (t + 1)) v) =
      (((((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) * (lam - (t : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v)
def CoordinateCore (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∃ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, lam.toNat < t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) x y h
def Coordinates (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ((lam.toNat + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = lam + 1 ∧
  0 < lam.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Index lam) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
  Lowering lam x y h v ∧
  (∀ i : Index lam, e y v i.val ≠ 0) ∧
  CoordinateCore lam x y h v ∧
  DividedFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) (divided x) (divided y)
def LocalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  (iota p M).range = Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V) ∧
  Nonempty (Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (localizedImage p M : Set V) = ⊤ ∧
  (∀ r, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r) ∧
    RPreserves p M (divided x r) ∧ RPreserves p M (divided y r)) ∧
  Preserves M x ∧ Preserves M y ∧ Preserves M h ∧
  RPreserves p M x ∧ RPreserves p M y ∧ RPreserves p M h ∧
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a
def MatrixIdentities (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Index lam,
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    divided x (lam.toNat - i.val) * (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b i (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) * divided y (lam.toNat - j.val) =
      (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℂ) • E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) j ∧
    (∃ c : R p, (c : ℚ) = (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℚ) ∧ IsUnit c) ∧
    E lam b i j = MatrixWord lam (divided x) (divided y) i j ∧
    RPreserves p M (E lam b i j)
def CommonModule (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Index lam, Ji p M y v i.val = J p M y v) ∧
  Nontrivial (J p M y v) ∧ Module.Finite (R p) (J p M y v) ∧
  ∃ c : (Index lam → J p M y v) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M,
    ∀ g, iota p M (c g) = ∑ i : Index lam, (g i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def RationalLine (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (qmul p M y v) ∧
  (qmul p M y v).range = Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v : Set ℂ) ∧
  Module.Finite ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) = 1
def PrincipalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  RationalLine p M y v ∧ (∃ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b) ∧
  ∀ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b → BasisLift p lam M y v b
def TensorMaps (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (hp : CharP K p) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (kap : R p →+* K) : Prop :=
  letI : CharP K p := hp
  letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
  letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
    (psi : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
    (∀ (c : K) (m : M), phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
    (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), psi (c ⊗ₜ[R p] u) =
      c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (ModN.mkQ p u)) ∧
    (∀ (f : Module.End ℤ M) (z : VK K M),
      phi (f.baseChange K z) = (f.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K (phi z)) ∧
    (∀ f : Module.End (R p) (MR p M),
      ∃ fbar : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
        (∀ u, fbar (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f u)) ∧
        ∀ z, psi (f.baseChange K z) = fbar.baseChange K (psi z))
def ScalarReduction (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (hp : CharP K p) (kap : R p →+* K),
    (∀ (r : R p) (a b : ℤ), b ≠ 0 → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b →
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ) → kap r = (a : K) / (b : K)) ∧
    TensorMaps p K hp M kap
def ReducedBasis (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
  ∃ (beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M)) (b : ℂ),
    Principal p M y v b ∧
    (∃ (kap : R p →+* K),
      letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
      ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
        (c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)),
        (∀ (s : K) (m : M), phi (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
        (∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val) ∧
        ∀ i, phi (beta i) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R p] (c i)) ∧
    Module.finrank K (VK K M) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
    GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)
def ReducedUnits (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat → (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  (∀ j : Index lam, (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
    (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat →
      (a.X r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.x.baseChange K) ^ r ∧
      (a.Y r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.y.baseChange K) ^ r) ∧
    ∀ beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M),
      GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K) →
      ∀ i j k : Index lam,
        MatrixWord lam (fun r => (a.X r).baseChange K) (fun r => (a.Y r).baseChange K) i j (beta k) =
          if j = k then beta i else 0

end SL2Reduction
open SL2Reduction

H003 retains finite dimension, all three commutators, a highest vector of weight λ and irreducibility under the generating actions; this is the operator presentation of the given sl₂-module, with the specified v retained separately in H004. λ remains an integer. Under H002, Index λ = Fin(λ.toNat+1) identifies bijectively with {i∈ℤ | 0≤i≤λ}; natural differences are used only inside this range. M is a ℤ-submodule of V; H005 supplies an arbitrary integer basis that is also a complex basis, and stability under every divided power. R is the ℤ-subalgebra of ℚ generated by the displayed prime-to-p fractions, with its exact original carrier established by T005; it is not assumed to be the whole ℚ. MR=R⊗ℤM and iota is the actual scalar multiplication lift; identifying with its image is justified only by N002. J_i and J are preimages of that image under c↦c e_i. qmul is the actual multiplication map ℚ⊗R J→ℂ. Scalar-first VK=K⊗ℤM is the same source tensor construction with factors swapped; T014 uses this convention throughout. ModN(MR,p) is the quotient by the image of multiplication by p. LatticeOps carries the actual restrictions, and Agrees specifies each value, rather than adding any action assumption. The target constructs these unique restrictions and states nonzero VK and every K-submodule invariant under x,y,h is bottom or top. Proposition-valued definitions only package displayed obligations; none proves them. Endomorphism multiplication is composition, integer coefficients are cast to the indicated field, and all factorials/choose arguments are natural numbers. Inspected pinned APIs: CharP K p asserts exactly (n:K)=0 iff p divides n, rather than merely p·1=0. Module.End multiplication is f.comp g, and Basis.coord is the coefficient function from its finitely-supported coordinate equivalence. LinearMap.liftBaseChange sends s⊗m to s•f(m), while LinearMap.baseChange sends s⊗m to s⊗f(m).
